rated_messages.input_message: Take a deep breath and let it out slowly. Notice that you are completely OK for this one breath. Do it again.
If you're stuck at home and physical activity doesn't interest you, try gaming, needlework, drawing, or journaling.
Keep picturing yourself getting home later today knowing that you've gained a smoke-free day. It's nearly a reality!
If you get urges, remind yourself that cigarettes did that to you. If you go back to them, they will keep making you suffer. Now you are breaking free.

Remind yourself that by staying quit, you'll be freeing yourself from the constant cycle of cigarette, nicotine withdrawal, feeling stressed as a result and wanting another cigarette. Keep going and this will be a thing of the past!

Add the phrase “I’m having the thought that…” in front of your unhelpful thoughts. For example, “I’m having the thought that I need a cigarette.” Your thoughts are not always true or helpful! They are just thoughts.
What can you do right now to break the automatic habit of smoking to help you feel better? Pause. Close your eyes. And take 10 slow breaths.

Think about your hero, or someone you admire. What do you admire about them? Often our heroes are people who struggle and succeed in difficult circumstances. Now's the chance to be your own hero - by not smoking despite the challenges of stress and strong urges!
Picture the people or things you care deeply about. On a scale of 0-10, how willing are you to let this urge pass for those reasons?
If you have trouble resisting a craving when other smokers are around, try carrying a water bottle and taking a sip every time you want to ask for a cig.
